text:
marta_fin: Heads-up — customer (VectorCloud Inc.) submitted a copy of a Texas resale certificate and is asking us to apply a sales-tax exemption to their upcoming SaaS invoice (INV-2024-708).
devon_sales: link to customer portal: https://app.redwood.com/customers/vectorcloud/invoices/INV-2024-708

marta_fin: they uploaded a PDF named TX-Resale-VectorCloud-2024.pdf. claiming purchases of platform access are resale for embedding into their product. subtotal = $18,450, recurring.
oscar_tax: Quick Q: do we classify their usage as taxable tangible software or non-taxable B2B service in TX? Texas tends to tax SaaS in many cases unless resold as a separate product. Need to review their certificate and check our product mapping.
amy_ops: Where do we store accepted resale certs? I remember we require the signed Form 01-339 (Texas) and we store a copy in VendDocs.

marta_fin: uploaded file to VendDocs and attached to bill.com. asking for guidance on acceptance.

compliance-bot: Automated check: certificate type detected=Resale Certificate (Texas Form 01-339). File metadata: signer=Evelyn Park, title=VP Finance, date_signed=2024-10-30. Certificate contains seller name 'Redwood Inference, Inc.' and purchaser description 'Tangible personal property for resale, includes software'.

oscar_tax: Bot found seller name match — good. Next step: confirm VectorCloud's evidence of resale: do they have a listed NAICS or demo showing they embed our API in a customer-facing product? If not, we need a signed purchaser declaration on the certificate and a business description. Also check nexus: do we have any taxable presence in TX for this product?
devon_sales: They do list NAICS 518210 (Data Processing, Hosting) — i'll ask product to confirm how they're reselling.

marta_fin: operational ask: if we accept, do we zero-rate the invoice now or hold until we verify usage category?
oscar_tax: Hold until we confirm usage category and that certificate applies to the billed items. If their purchase is strictly for internal use (analytics) it's likely not resale. If they re-bundle and invoice their customers, certificate may apply.
amy_ops: For timing, we can place the invoice on hold for 5 business days and notify customer. If they provide additional proof (screenshot of product page showing our offering listed as part of their product) we can process.

devon_sales: i'll request a product doc and a signed purchaser declaration confirming resale within 2 business days. cc @Evelyn Park.
marta_fin: noted — i'll mark invoice INV-2024-708 as 'pending tax evidence' in bill.com and set reminder for 5 days.

oscar_tax: If they supply Form 01-339 + purchaser declaration + evidence of resale, we accept and apply exemption to future invoices; for the current billing period we'll do a credit if evidence is retroactive and covers the invoice dates. Document retention: store copy in VendDocs and record acceptance in tax log.

marta_fin: thanks. one more: do we need to collect a seller's permit from them?
oscar_tax: No — seller's permit not required from purchaser. We need the signed purchaser certificate and supporting evidence. Also note: if we later determine it's not resale, we may need to self-assess and remit tax plus interest.

devon_sales: pinged Evelyn for product proof.

marta_fin: thanks all :thumbsup:

system_bot: Invoice INV-2024-708 uploaded by vectorcloud-billing at 2024-11-20 15:04 UTC.
